results.fact: Church Lake elevation / gain from trailhead
results.correct_value: Path CLIMBS ~400 ft (trailhead ~4,800 ft, over a ~5,200 ft rise, to the lake at ~5,146 ft); trailhead is ~4,800 ft, not 4,900
results.evidence: The Church Lake path climbs, it does not drop: one trail database gives trailhead 4,803 ft, high point 5,205 ft and 402 ft of gain over 0.6 mi, and a 2023 trip report gives ~0.7 mi and 400 ft of gain; the state fish-and-wildlife lake listing puts Church Lake at 5,146 ft. USGS 3DEP elevations at the stored pins read 4,823 ft at the trailhead and 5,128 ft at the lake. So the approach's ~400 ft (gross, over the rise) and the lake waypoint's 5,150 are right; the beta's 'drops' and the trailhead's 4,900 ft are wrong.

results.fact: Which side of the lake and basin
results.evidence: Trip reports agree only that parties keep LEFT after the lake and climb the left rim of the basin to Point 6066; none gives a compass direction. USGS elevation sampling suggests 6066 lies south-southwest of the lake with the summit ridge on the basin's west side, which could fit either reading depending on the arrival direction, so east vs west is not settled by two sources. No patch.

The hiking association's Church Lake page says the route is not an official trail but a user-built, often overgrown path; a trip report notes motorcycles have worn it in. Overview, beta, approach, waypoints, access and the approach variant all call it unmaintained; only what_to_bring says 'maintained'.

results.correct_value: Point 6066 is a knoll / subsidiary high point (~25-30 ft below Bearpaw), not a col
results.evidence: A trip report describes 6066 as an unnamed peak labelled 6066, about 30 ft lower than Bearpaw on the same ridge. USGS 3DEP sampling at the stored pin (6,066 ft) shows every surrounding point on a ~150 m grid is lower (5,600-5,950 ft), i.e. a local summit, not a saddle. The row's own waypoint name ('Knoll') and 'drop slightly' toward the summit block agree.

patches.find: THE 6,066 FT SADDLE IS THE TOP OF THE APPROACH, AND IT IS A COL: a broad low point on the ridge separating the Church Lake basin from the summit block, with ground falling away on the far side. Arriving somewhere you can see down both sides is the confirmation.
patches.replace: THE 6,066 FT KNOLL IS THE TOP OF THE APPROACH: a broad high point on the ridge separating the Church Lake basin from the summit block, only a few tens of feet lower than the true summit. Arriving somewhere the ground falls away on every side is the confirmation.

results.correct_value: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District), outside the Mount Baker Wilderness; camp at existing Church Lake sites
results.evidence: The Forest Service's official wilderness boundary layer returns no wilderness at the trailhead, Church Lake, Point 6066 or the summit (a control point near Damfino Lakes returns Mount Baker Wilderness). A trip report states the area is National Forest, not Wilderness, which is why motorbikes use the path. The Chain Lakes are on the Heather Meadows side and unrelated; the hiking association asks visitors to use existing campsites at Church Lake.
